The address is not proven by this. 422 validation_failed (for the field), weak_password (with rule: too_short and minLength, too_long and maxLength, letter_and_digit, personal or breached); 403 sign_up_closed (invite only), consent_required (with the consents still asked), risk_refused, sign_in_paused or method_refused (the role for new sign-ups); 409 already_exists.

POST /v1/setup-links/lookup.summary: What a setup page shows before the password
POST /v1/setup-links/lookup.description: For your setup page (and the sign-in widget’s): whether the link works, and while it does, whom to greet. The link’s code goes in the body, never in an address, so its secret stays out of request logs. Answers valid with the person’s display name, the last 4 digits of their phone number (null without one; never the whole number or the email address) and when the link ends; else expired (past its end), used (the password was set with it), canceled (a newer link replaced it, or staff declined its request) or invalid. Only a code whose secret matches learns anything: an unknown or wrong code always answers invalid, so the lookup tells nothing about other links or people. A link is known 30 days past its end; later it is invalid. Rate-limited per visitor like the accept route.

POST /v1/sign-in/phone/code.description: Works while Phone code or Phone + password is on. POST /v1/sign-in/phone.description: Proves the number. It opens only an account whose number was proven (an account that holds the number unproven loses it to this proof, and the sign-in goes on as for a number without an account; a sign-in code from staff still opens its own user). A number without an account signs up with the sign-up members (a new user without a name gets your newUserName). 422 code_invalid (5 wrong codes use the code up). returnTo.description: Your page: https on your website’s domain (a local page while testing).

remember.description: Remember me (the role decides whether it is asked).

POST /v1/sign-in/exchange.summary: Exchange a Google, Apple or Facebook hand-over code for the sign-in
POST /v1/sign-in/exchange.description: The provider proved the address: a known provider account, or an account whose address was proven before, is opened; else an account is made. 422 code_invalid when the code is not valid, used or older than 5 minutes. 403 blocked, pending_approval, sign_in_paused (the detail is your paused text) or method_refused (the user’s role); 403 consent_required (with the consents still asked) until they are given in consents.

code.description: The ss_accounts_code value of the address fragment.

consents.description: The consents the visitor checked, { key: true } (Consents): every required agreement not given in its current version must be true, else 403 consent_required with consents: [{ key, label, url, version }]; false refuses an optional one.

POST /v1/sign-in/two-step.summary: The two-step code, or a recovery code, of a sign-in
POST /v1/sign-in/two-step.description: For status two_step: a code from the authenticator app or one recovery code (each works once). For status two_step_setup: the first code from the app; the answer then carries 10 recovery codes. Wrong codes count toward the user’s lock like wrong passwords (except while setting up) and 5 wrong codes end the step: 422 code_invalid; 423 locked (with lockedUntil).

recoveryCode.description: Instead of code: one recovery code (spaces and dashes are ignored).

POST /v1/invites/accept.summary: Accept an invite and sign in
POST /v1/invites/accept.description: The invite’s token comes from the link (#ss_accounts_invite=<token>). The account becomes active, its email address (else phone number) proven; a password is set when the method is on (Email + password for a user with an email address, Phone + password for one with a phone number). 422 code_invalid (not valid, used or expired), weak_password, validation_failed (name). 403 blocked, pending_approval, sign_in_paused (the detail is your paused text) or method_refused (the user’s role); 403 consent_required (with the consents still asked) until they are given in consents.

name.description: Replaces the name the invite gave.

remember.description: Remember me (the role decides whether it is asked).

deviceId.description: A random id the browser keeps (risk checks count accounts per device).

consents.description: The consents the visitor checked, { key: true } (Consents): every required agreement not given in its current version must be true, else 403 consent_required with consents: [{ key, label, url, version }]; false refuses an optional one.

POST /v1/session/refresh.description: Answers a new sign-in and a new refresh token. The token renewed less than 30 seconds ago gets the same new pair (parallel renewals, a retry); presented later, it ends the session. With the role’s sessionRolling, the session’s end moves to its length from now. 401 signed_out when the session ended or the user is blocked or not active.

POST /v1/session/sign-out.description: Answers 204 whatever the token: an unknown or ended session changes nothing.

GET /v1/me.description: Send the sign-in in SS-Sign-In (401 signed_out when it is not valid, its session ended or the user is blocked).

GET /v1/lookup/me.summary: The signed-in user, for another product
GET /v1/lookup/me.description: The same answer as GET /v1/me, for another product of the website that holds the signed-in person's Accounts sign-in (Ecommerce asks for the shopper's name and city). Called with the server token or with a link key that holds the scope me.read, and the sign-in in SS-Sign-In (401 signed_out when it is not valid, its session ended or the user is blocked).

PATCH /v1/me.summary: Change the signed-in user’s name, custom fields or addresses
PATCH /v1/me.description: Send the sign-in in SS-Sign-In (401 signed_out when it is not valid, its session ended or the user is blocked). The email address and phone number change only by signing in with them. 422 validation_failed for the field; 403 feature_off for custom while Custom fields is off.

addresses.description: The whole list (at most 10; keepOneAddress refuses an empty list once the user has one); the first is the default unless one is marked.

GET /v1/me/sessions.description: Send the sign-in in SS-Sign-In (401 signed_out when it is not valid, its session ended or the user is blocked). Open sessions, most recently used first.

DELETE /v1/me/sessions/:id.description: Send the sign-in in SS-Sign-In (401 signed_out when it is not valid, its session ended or the user is blocked). 404 not_found when the session is not the user’s or already ended.

POST /v1/me/sign-out-everywhere.summary: Sign out of every device, this one too
POST /v1/me/sign-out-everywhere.description: Send the sign-in in SS-Sign-In (401 signed_out when it is not valid, its session ended or the user is blocked). Sign-ins already given end within 15 minutes.

PUT /v1/me/password.summary: Set or change the signed-in user’s password
PUT /v1/me/password.description: Send the sign-in in SS-Sign-In (401 signed_out when it is not valid, its session ended or the user is blocked). Users with an email address while Email + password is on, else users with a phone number while Phone + password is on (422 validation_failed otherwise), with that method’s rules (422 weak_password). Every other device signs in again. 401 sign_in_failed when current is wrong. Without a password, the change needs a fresh code (confirmCode); 422 code_invalid for a missing, wrong or used code. 423 locked while wrong passwords hold the account.

current.description: The current password; required when the user has one (a wrong one counts toward the lock like a wrong sign-in password).

confirmCode.description: Instead, for a user without a password: a fresh code from POST /v1/me/confirm-code, used up by this call.

POST /v1/me/two-step/setup.description: Send the sign-in in SS-Sign-In (401 signed_out when it is not valid, its session ended or the user is blocked). The secret waits 10 minutes for POST /v1/me/two-step/enable. 409 conflict while two-step sign-in is on (and its secret still opens). Needs the current password, or for a user without one a fresh code (confirmCode), as the password change does (401 sign_in_failed, 422 code_invalid). The challenge is for POST /v1/me/two-step/enable only: POST /v1/sign-in/two-step refuses it.

current.description: The current password; required when the user has one (a wrong one counts toward the lock like a wrong sign-in password).

POST /v1/me/two-step/enable.summary: Turn two-step sign-in on with the first code
POST /v1/me/two-step/enable.description: Send the sign-in in SS-Sign-In (401 signed_out when it is not valid, its session ended or the user is blocked). 422 code_invalid for a wrong code (5 wrong codes end the setup) or a setup that is not this user’s or has expired.

recoveryCodes.description: Only right after two-step sign-in was set up: 10 recovery codes, shown once.

POST /v1/me/two-step/disable.description: Send the sign-in in SS-Sign-In (401 signed_out when it is not valid, its session ended or the user is blocked). Answers 204 when it is off already. 403 two_step_required when the user’s role requires it; 422 code_invalid. Needs the current password or a fresh code (confirmCode) as well as the code from the app (401 sign_in_failed, 422 code_invalid).

current.description: The current password; required when the user has one (a wrong one counts toward the lock like a wrong sign-in password).

confirmCode.description: Instead, for a user without a password: a fresh code from POST /v1/me/confirm-code, used up by this call.

Wrong codes count toward the lock (422 code_invalid); 423 locked (with lockedUntil); 409 conflict while two-step sign-in is off.

recoveryCode.description: Instead of code: one recovery code.

recoveryCodes.description: Only right after two-step sign-in was set up: 10 recovery codes, shown once.

POST /v1/admin/role-requests/:id/invite.summary: Invite the person of a pending request (Users admin widget)
POST /v1/admin/role-requests/:id/invite.description: Creates their user, or finds the user with that phone number (else email address), and answers a setup link for your staff to send, unless the user already has a password (the request is then completed). The role is given at the invite, or with Role requests → giveRoleAt set to completion when the request is completed (a new user has the default role until then, an existing user keeps theirs). 409 contact_unverified when that user never proved the phone or email and someone signed in to it (check with the person, confirm it on their user or remove that account, then invite again); 409 conflict when the request is not pending, its role is gone, another user has the contact, or the user's role ranks above the request's (a user has one role and a request never lowers it: change the role on their user if that is what you want); 404 not_found. 403 forbidden by the guards when the call names its acting user (SS-Actor-Id) or comes with a ticket: nobody changes their own role, blocks or deletes themselves, touches a user whose role ranks above theirs or gives a role ranking above theirs, and the last unblocked Owner stays.

POST /v1/import/:collection.description: collection: roles and fields (found by key), users (usr_…), requests (rrq_…) or copies, in that order (a user’s role must exist); 404 not_found for another. Send application/x-ndjson, one record of Accounts’ own shape per line, at most 1,000 records or 4 MB (413 payload_too_large; 415 unsupported_media_type). Each record replaces the stored one with its key; an unknown field (websiteId too) refuses the record by name. A user's roleSince defaults to its createdAt; a user or request without createdAt keeps the one stored, else gets the time of the import. Users keep their password hashes (bcrypt, pbkdf2$… with the imported_password_pepper connection, scrypt$…) and two-step secrets (sealed at once); an email address or phone number another user holds is refused. Nothing is sent.

dryRun.description: Check (or count) only: nothing is written.

response.description: What was (or, in a dry run, would be) written.

id.description: The record’s key (null when the line is not a record).

path.description: A JSON Pointer in the record.

POST /v1/import/:collection/prune.summary: Remove imported records the source no longer has
POST /v1/import/:collection/prune.description: Removes the records an import wrote whose key lies after after and up to through (open ends when left out) and is not in keep, at most 1,000 per call (more: true: call again). Send the source’s keys sorted (byte order of their UTF-8), cut into calls. Only records an import wrote are removed: records made in Accounts itself stay, and a removed ready-made role comes back with its defaults. 422 validation_failed for keep; 413 payload_too_large over 1,000 keys.

dryRun.description: Check (or count) only: nothing is written.

keep.description: The keys (id, or key for roles and fields) the source has in this range.

removed.description: In a dry run: how many would go.

keys.description: The keys removed (in a dry run: the first 1,000 that would go).

more.description: More records of the range are to be removed: call again.

POST /v1/import/finish.description: Accounts derives nothing: it reports users whose role does not exist (they act as customer until it is imported) and role requests whose user is gone.

GET /v1/import/status.summary: What the import holds now (ss-import verify)

totals.description: The sums the importer compares with the source: users.staff (role with a permission), users.withPassword, users.twoStep, users.role.<key> for each role in use, requests.pending.

POST /v1/me/confirm-code.summary: Send a fresh code to prove the person (users without a password)
POST /v1/me/confirm-code.description: Send the sign-in in SS-Sign-In (401 signed_out when it is not valid, its session ended or the user is blocked). For a user without a password: a 6-digit code goes to the proven email address (else the proven phone number), and the password and two-step changes take it as confirmCode. The usual code limits apply (429 code_cooldown with retryAt, or code_limit). 409 conflict when the user has a password (type it instead) or neither address nor number was proven.
